name: Live rolling-buffer granular processor with per-grain behaviour modes: interval 'mosaic' clouds, per-grain pitch glide, reverse+wow smear, ghost-grain bloom, LFO tide, fixed-position constellation patterns and orbiting read head
goal: Turn a constantly recording one-bar buffer into a real-time granular effect for pads, keys, vocals and guitar (insert with dry/wet or 100% wet send). It uses the standard grain controls (size, density, spray around the playhead, pitch in perfect-fifth steps, jitter, spread, stereo scatter, reverse chance, top-end smoothing), a tempo-synced grain trigger/size option, a quantised or auto-moving playhead, and a library of grain-scheduling behaviours a Web Audio granulator can implement: mosaic (grains pitched into chordal interval sets: fifths/major/minor/discordant), glide (each grain sweeps up in pitch over its own length with a curve), reverie (all grains reversed with tape-style wow), bloom (each grain spawns a later, quieter, slightly detuned ghost grain), tide (a global LFO swells and recedes playback rate), stars (grains drawn from fixed buffer positions in forward/reverse/pendulum/random patterns, looping each bar) and orbit (grains circling the write head with width and 'slop'). Delta vs our granular-buffer-core and frozen-buffer skills: live write/read buffer and the per-grain behaviour modes.

source.title: Celestine - A Realtime Granular Dream Machine (Full Walkthrough)
source.transcript_note: Developer walkthrough of a commercial Max for Live device. Long personal/pricing preamble and shop CTA dropped; modes kept as portable grain-scheduling recipes.

prerequisites: Granular engine reading a circular buffer that is continuously written (Web Audio: AudioWorklet ring buffer + grain scheduler, implementation note)
Optional wavefolder, bitcrusher and long hall reverb after the grains

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Melodic material (keys, vocals, guitar, pads) or percussion

inputs.name: buffer_length
inputs.description: One bar of the current tempo

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: grain | mosaic | glide | reverie | bloom | tide | stars | orbit

outputs.name: granular_texture
outputs.description: Real-time granular cloud derived from what is playing right now

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
The buffer is a fleeting rolling recording, not storage: pausing record ('live' off) holds the content only until the next playback start.
Read and write heads must not collide inside the ring buffer or you get glitches. Keep a guard distance between them (developer's stated engine problem; the fix is not described).
Mode behaviours are described qualitatively; parameter amounts are by ear.
Pricing, story and shop links in the source are omitted.

steps.action: Insert the processor on a track (balance dry/wet) or on a send at 100% wet. A one-bar ring buffer records whatever plays, and grains are read from it continuously.
steps.expect: Grains follow the live input with no pre-recorded sample

steps.action: Set the base cloud: size (grain length), density (grains at once, sparse to dense), spray (how far from the playhead grains may be fetched; 0 = exactly at the playhead), pitch in perfect-fifth steps, jitter (slight per-grain pitch warble, good for cloudy drones), spread (any pitch per grain, extreme), stereo (grains scattered around the field; presenter keeps it high), reverse chance, and smooth (roll off top end if grains get clicky).
steps.expect: A dense or sparse cloud with controlled pitch and stereo scatter

steps.action: Playhead: scrub manually, or quantise it to eight positions (eighth notes in the one-bar buffer) to land on downbeat transients, or set a move rate (slow/fast, forward or reverse) to scan automatically.
steps.expect: Grains drawn from chosen rhythmic positions or a moving scan

steps.action: Sync sub-mode: when synced, grains fire on time divisions (e.g. 16ths) and size switches to note lengths. Each behaviour mode below has a free and a synced variant.
steps.expect: Grains snap to the grid; percussive, rhythmic output

steps.action: Mosaic: pitch successive grains into chordal intervals (a couple at root, then +7, +12 …) with a soft bloom and slight lo-fi. Pick an interval set: fifths, major, minor or discordant. Reduce density; add jitter or spread. Good for pads with lots of reverb.
steps.expect: Harmonic cloud chords built from the input

steps.action: Glide: each grain glides up in pitch (micro-portamento). Glide depth sets the interval; grain size sets how long it takes, and a shape control sets the curve. Long grains give a smooth effect; percussive input makes a texture generator.

Reverie: force all grains into reverse and add tape-like wow/flutter (wow depth control) with a slight lo-fi tone; longer sizes give stretched tape-echo smears. Reverse chance has no further effect here.
Bloom: every triggered grain spawns a secondary ghost grain that enters slightly later, quieter and subtly detuned. Raise density and size for overlapping halos.
Tide: a global LFO makes all grains swell and recede in playback rate together. Long size = ambient breathing; short size = tremolo-like.
steps.expect: Organic push-pull breathing of the texture

steps.action: Stars: ignore the heads and read grains from fixed positions in the buffer. Spray becomes a pattern selector (forward, reverse, pendulum, random), which cycles each bar into recognisable melodic or rhythmic fragment loops.

Orbit: grains circle the write head in a spiralling orbit. Spray becomes orbit width, plus a slop control for imperfection/lo-fi. Works best at slow tempos and lower densities and plays alongside the dry signal like its own loop.
steps.expect: Rotating texture revolving around the 'present' audio

steps.action: Finish inside the grain path: a wavefolder or bitcrusher with its own mix for grit, then a simple hall reverb (decay + mix); long decay feels almost frozen. Revisit playhead/spray/sync after picking a mode, since each changes the mode's result a lot.

verification: With spray at 0 and move off, grains come only from the playhead position.
Synced mode places grains on the chosen division, audibly on the grid.
Mosaic output contains the chosen interval set (e.g. root/+7/+12) when fed a single note.
Bloom shows delayed, quieter duplicate grains; tide shows periodic rate swells.
